claims: Required CI job `Test Peg rule definitions` fails — `alerts/rules/peg-message-templates.tf:13-15` the new title template contains neither `Annotations.summary` nor `Annotations.resolved_summary`; `alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69` still asserts both are present

`Error → Alerting` now discards the breach's measured cause and the clear reports the wrong magnitude — `peg-alert-events.ts:109-115` returns `error-recovered-alerting`, which `isOpening` (line 318) treats as a closing transition on the error lane, so the alert lane never opens; the later `Alerting → Normal` is orphaned into `unpairedCleared`
After a datasource blip during a live breach, Recent alerts reports the deviation as 5 bps instead of the 31 bps that actually fired, and drops the duration
Canonical runbook now contradicts shipped behaviour — `docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:118-119` "Slack titles use the severity icon plus that summary" but titles are now icon-only

`docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:132-133` says the history backend "does not read Pending or canceled transitions" and reads only fired and resolved transitions, but it now also reads `Error` and `Error →` recoveries; reversing that contract without amending the sentence leaves operators following the previous decision

`Alerting → Error → Normal` leaves the alert cycle open forever — `peg-alert-events.ts:344-352` closes only the error lane, so the panel simultaneously says monitoring recovered and the breach is live when Grafana is Normal

`Error → Pending` is neither queried nor classified — `peg-alert-events.ts:109-115` returns `null` for it and `route.ts:51-54` only derives `previous=Error&current=Normal`, so the `Grafana could not evaluate…` entry never gets a recovery

Source-less rules are described as price-source rules — `peg-alert-events.ts:230-234` → `pegAlertSourceName("")` returns `"Price source"` (`peg-alert-copy.ts:47-49`) for structural and heartbeat rules where `source = ""`

Query fan-out doubled back to four, and `Promise.all` makes each one fatal — `route.ts:63-64` + `115-122`: any single rejection → 502 for the whole endpoint, so an Error-query hiccup now blanks the breach history that used to render fine
Peak read budget also goes 2 × 4 MB → 4 × 4 MB
This may reintroduce the outage that #1875 fixed when it cut this exact fan-out from four to two under the title "restore alert history availability"

Three fault tests now pass through a path that cannot occur in production — `route.test.ts:819, 832, 846` `.mockResolvedValue(json(stateFrame([])))` evaluates `json(...)` once so all three concurrent calls share one `Response`; `readBoundedGrafanaResponse` (`grafana-read.ts:65`) locks the stream and the second and third calls throw `TypeError`, so every one of these tests yields 502 whether or not the guards work
`recent-alerts.test.tsx:193` — `not.toContain("sell price is below peg")` is vacuous; no production explanation emits that string
`alert-rules-lint.test.mjs:1215-1220` — the `indexOf` slice and the new link assertions search the whole file rather than the message resource; brittle
`https://monitoring.mento.org/peg-monitoring` is hardcoded six times in `peg-message-templates.tf:29,46`; a local would be tidier
Monitoring-failure entries compete for the same `PEG_ALERTS_MAX_EVENTS = 4` slots as breaches (`route.ts:22`), so a flapping datasource can push real peg breaches off Recent alerts entirely
